images.caption: Tomb monument of Dame Mary Page (d.1728) in Bunhill Fields burial ground: north side. Inscription reads: "Here lies Dame Mary Page relict of Sir Gregory Page Bart. She departed this life March 11th 1728 in the 56th year of her age. In 67 months she was tap'd 66 times, Had taken away 240 gallons of water without ever repining at her case or ever fearing the operation."

images.caption: Bunhill Fields Burial Ground The name 'Bunhill' is a corruption of 'Bone Hill' - it is thought that burial and the disposal of human bones have taken place here or hereabouts for about 1000 years.  At the end of the seventeenth century it began to be used formally as a burial ground for dissenters - mainly nonconformists - and many notable personages lie here at rest, including John Bunyan and Daniel Defoe. In the mid-nineteenth century it was closed to further burials.  See also Bunhill_Fields.   There are many fine old trees here also, including plane and sycamore.
